triggers: a kernel on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120) risks the '11. Increasing BV per CTA can *decrease* ncu Max BW %' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on NVIDIA Blackwell GeForce/workstation (RTX PRO 5000 / SM120): 11. Increasing BV per CTA can *decrease* ncu Max BW %

problem.statement: CuTeDSL GDN Decode on sm_120 — Pitfalls -- 11. Increasing BV per CTA can *decrease* ncu Max BW %

payload.attempted: After V13 hits 87.7% Max BW, double BV (8 → 16) to amortize fixed per-CTA overhead and (you assume) push closer to peak.
payload.lesson: For ncu **DRAM Throughput %** specifically, larger tiles can be a regression. To push the *metric*, push toward zero L1 hit (every load `cg`). To push *wall-clock*, follow the regular roofline rules.

established_fact.mechanism: A bigger tile means more threads in the same CTA share L1 lines for boundary loads. More L1 reuse = fewer DRAM bytes attributed = lower "DRAM throughput %". The kernel hasn't actually slowed down; the metric just changed its denominator.

payload.observed: Max BW drops to 87.24% (slightly worse), wall-clock unchanged. L1 hit rate jumps from 33% → 53%.
payload.root_cause: A bigger tile means more threads in the same CTA share L1 lines for boundary loads. More L1 reuse = fewer DRAM bytes attributed = lower "DRAM throughput %". The kernel hasn't actually slowed down; the metric just changed its denominator.
